violations.description: The CI workflow's push trigger only targets feature/** branches, so pushes to the default branch main are never validated by CI.
violations.evidence: ci.yml lines 3-7: 'on: pull_request: branches: [main]' and 'push: branches: [feature/**]'. The repository default branch is main (git_status). A direct push/merge commit to main does not match any push branch filter, so CI (lint-free but test+Docker validation) is skipped on main.
violations.recommendation: Add main to the push branch filter, e.g. 'push: branches: [main, "feature/**"]', so every commit landing on the default branch is validated.

violations.description: No linting or formatting tooling is configured or executed anywhere in the repository.
violations.evidence: The tracked file set is exactly: .dockerignore, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, .gitignore, Assignment1_Report.pdf, Dockerfile, README.md, VERSION, app.py, requirements.txt, tests/test_app.py. There is no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, ruff.toml, .flake8, .pre-commit-config.yaml, or Makefile, and requirements.txt (fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic, httpx, pytest) declares no linter/formatter. Neither ci.yml nor release.yml contains a lint/format step (parse_workflow reports 'lint: none' for both).
violations.recommendation: Add ruff (or flake8/black) with a minimal config and a lint step in ci.yml so style/quality issues are caught automatically.

violations.description: Version identifiers are defined as constants (APP_VERSION from VERSION, MODEL_VERSION) but the /health handler hardcodes the same literals instead of using them, leaving MODEL_VERSION unused and the version duplicated in three places.
violations.evidence: app.py:14 'APP_VERSION = read_version()', app.py:15 'MODEL_VERSION = "model-1"', but the health handler at app.py:43-48 builds the payload with literal strings 'application_version': '1.1.0' and 'model_version': 'model-1'. MODEL_VERSION is never referenced anywhere; search_code shows only the definition and the literal. VERSION file is '1.1.0'. A future VERSION bump changes APP_VERSION/api docs but not the health response.
violations.recommendation: Use the constants in the health payload, e.g. 'application_version': APP_VERSION, 'model_version': MODEL_VERSION, so version reporting has a single source of truth.
